summary: The note explains the 'three points for a win' scoring standard, widely used in sports leagues and group tournaments, especially association football. Under this system a win earns three points, a loss earns none, and a draw gives each team one point. Because wins are worth more relative to draws, teams with more wins can outrank teams with fewer wins but more draws.
one_line: Explains the three-points-for-a-win scoring system used in football leagues and group tournaments, where wins are valued above draws.
key_facts: Three points for a win is a standard used in many sports leagues and group tournaments.
The system is especially used in association football.
Three points are awarded to the team winning a match.
No points are awarded to the losing team.
If a game is drawn, each team receives one point.
The system places additional value on wins compared to draws.
Teams with a higher number of wins may rank higher in tables than teams with fewer wins but more draws.

entities.name: Association football
entities.role: sport in which the three-points-for-a-win standard is especially used
